en: Dependent on a state that has both applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and is not a root-cause (*na-hetu*), there arises a state that has neither applied thought nor sustained thought (*nasavitakkasavicāra*) and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. In the case of root-condition, there are fifteen; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), there are fifteen.

Dependent on a state that has both applied thought and sustained thought and is not a root-cause, there arises a state that has neither applied thought nor mere sustained thought (*naavitakkavicāramatta*) and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition.

(Abbreviated. In the case of root-condition, there are twenty-eight; in the case of object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), there are twenty-eight; in the case of predominance-condition (*adhipati*), [there are twenty-eight].
In the case of the prenascence and repetition conditions, there are nineteen [answers]... [and so on] ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition, there are twenty-eight.
